question: Which remaining Android node powers should OpenClaw accept now: narrow device-control commands, an ADB-style command surface, arbitrary Kotlin/dynamic execution, or only a generic node-tool API first?
rationale: The remaining work changes what a connected phone can let the model read or execute, so automation cannot safely choose the trust model, sandbox, approval prompts, or core-versus-plugin boundary.

options.title: Split and gate narrow commands
options.body: Define small device-control commands first, make privacy or control actions explicit opt-in through existing node command policy, and defer ADB/dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

options.title: Route through generic node tools
options.body: Treat ADB and dynamic execution as dependent on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8287 so Android does not grow one-off model-visible execution paths.

options.title: Decline arbitrary execution
options.body: Keep Android limited to reviewed native command handlers and reject arbitrary Kotlin/ADB execution unless a maintainer sponsors a hardened sandbox design.

recommendation.title: Split and gate narrow commands
recommendation.body: Define small device-control commands first, make privacy or control actions explicit opt-in through existing node command policy, and defer ADB/dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the clearest recent merged history and product comments across Android node commands and per-device session behavior.
